lead: Once the cervix is fully dilated, the fetus rotates and flexes through the curved bony pelvis in a precise biomechanical sequence known as the cardinal movements. In this illustrated guide to second stage of labor anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including complete cervical dilation, pelvic inlet, ischial spines, pelvic outlet—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Once the cervix is fully dilated, the fetus rotates and flexes through the curved bony pelvis in a precise biomechanical sequence known as the cardinal movements. The second stage begins at complete cervical dilation and ends at birth of the baby. In a typical vertex vaginal delivery, the presenting head descends and may flex and rotate to negotiate maternal pelvic dimensions, then extend beneath the pubic arch. questions.answer: It begins at complete cervical dilation and ends when the baby is born. The later delivery of placenta belongs to a distinct third stage.
